title: T5: Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer
hook: What if translation, classification, and summarization were all just text-in, text-out? T5 makes one model and one recipe handle them all.
key_points: Reframes every NLP task as text-to-text: the input is text and the output is text.
One encoder-decoder model and one training recipe cover many tasks at once.
Systematically studied transfer learning choices — objectives, data, and scale.
Pretrained on a large cleaned web corpus, then fine-tuned per task.
content_html: Raffel and colleagues proposed T5, which frames every NLP task — translation, classification, summarization, and more — as taking in text and producing text. That single formulation lets one encoder-decoder Transformer and one training recipe handle them all. The paper also ran a broad, systematic study of transfer learning, comparing pretraining objectives, datasets, and model sizes.
extra_html:
How it works

Instead of bolting a different output head onto the model for each task, T5 turns every task into a text generation problem. A prompt prefix tells the model what to do — for example, asking it to translate or to summarize — and the model writes the answer as text. It's pretrained on a large, cleaned web corpus with a fill-in-the-blank style objective, then fine-tuned on specific tasks while keeping the same text-to-text interface throughout.

Why it matters

Unifying tasks under one interface simplifies how you build and reuse models, and it foreshadowed the prompt-driven approach that later large language models adopted. Just as valuable, the paper's careful experiments gave the field a clearer, evidence-based picture of what actually drives transfer learning, rather than relying on folklore.

related.hook: What if a model read a sentence both directions at once? BERT did, by masking words and predicting them — and made pretrain-then-fine-tune the default recipe in NLP.
